newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:
Spokesmen Nico Wegter and Josep Coll i Carbo briefed on Tuesday's meeting of the General Affairs Council in Luxembourg.

Coll i Carbo said that PLO leader Yasser Arafat had been invited to go to Luxembourg and that a meeting could take place on Monday evening or afternoon. However, he was not able to confirm whether Arafat would attend.

Coll i Carbo said the Council would consider launching the second phase of the EU's procedure on the U.S. Helms Burton law on sanctions against Cuba. It would consist of opening a dispute panel within the World Trade Organisation.
Wegter said the Council would discuss the state of play in Bosnia-Herzogovina after the elections. The session would take place in the presence of Carl Bildt.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/864: Humanitarian aid: news in brief
- IP/96/865: Tadjikistan: Commission approves humanitarian aid package worth Ecu 1.42 million.

- IP/96/866: The Commission has given the green light to the proposed acquisition of control of the German credit insurance company Hermes Kreditversicherung-AG, Hamburg, by Alliance AG holding, Munich.
- IP/96/867: Fifth EU/Japan Summit - joint press statement.
- Spee/96/229: Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies at the Labour Party Congress.
- Spee/96/228 Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn at the colloquium on the challenges of living and working in the European Information Society: people first.
- Eurostat news release no 63/96: Under four million EU babies born in 1995.
